trials.notes: Used the correct WP_HTML_Tag_Processor for a flat attribute edit, called only documented APIs, walked tags with next_tag(), removed names returned by get_attribute_names_with_prefix(), and returned get_updated_html(). No _doing_it_wrong records.
Same documented and idiomatic pattern as the reference. The implementation avoids value parsing entirely, so boolean/empty/decoded attribute-value edge cases are not mishandled.
API usage is fully documented and appropriate. The function_exists wrapper is extra PHP structure but does not affect HTML API adherence or the hidden tests.

failure_analysis: All trials passed every hidden case: single-link, multiple-tags, multiple-matching-attributes, similar-prefixes-kept, uppercase-source-attribute, comments-untouched, and no-matches. There are no failed hidden cases to attribute to documentation gaps. The docs worked well here because the Tag Processor overview explicitly recommends it for flat attribute/class edits and byte-preserving output; the usage section shows direct construction with new WP_HTML_Tag_Processor; next_tag() documents walking all real tag openers while skipping comment text and incomplete tokens; get_attribute_names_with_prefix() documents lowercase returned names and case-insensitive matching; remove_attribute() supplies the needed mutation; and get_updated_html() is clearly presented as the retrieval method after queued edits. The main near-miss is that get_attribute_names_with_prefix() does not explicitly state the empty-array case for a matched tag with no matching attributes, though all candidates handled the nullable return safely anyway.

doc_gaps.problem: The return contract says array|null and shows null when no tag opener is matched, but it does not explicitly say that a matched tag with no matching attributes returns an empty array.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a sentence such as: "Returns an empty array when currently matched on a tag opener but no attribute name starts with the prefix; returns null only when no tag opener is currently matched."

doc_gaps.problem: The docs say returned names are lowercase, but they do not explicitly state that these normalized names are safe to pass back into get_attribute(), set_attribute(), or remove_attribute() to target source attributes with different original casing.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Document that returned names are comparable normalized names and may be passed directly to attribute APIs; matching remains ASCII case-insensitive for HTML attributes.

doc_gaps.problem: The method docblock is terse and does not surface useful removal semantics that matter for bulk attribute operations, including case-insensitive name matching, no-op behavior for absent attributes, duplicate-attribute removal, and whitespace preservation side effects.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Expand the contract to describe these general behaviors and point to get_updated_html() for byte-preserving output, noting that surrounding whitespace is not currently pruned.
